cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a woman's cotton tube skirt (phasin) with polychrome horizontal stripes and a dark indigo lower panel — a garment type worn by Lahu and neighboring highland Tai-related groups in Myanmar/Thailand, consistent with the claimed Lahu attribution with no evidence pointing to a different culture.

physical.title: skirt
physical.summary: A woman's tube skirt, a phasin.  Made of five unequal sized pieces of tabby cotton cloth (paired warps) with polychrome bands (woven as stripes).  Top section [35 cms deep] has cream band (single warps), with evenly spaced polychrome bands on a red 'ground' below; red weft.  Middle section [29 cms] has more closely spaced polychrome bands, with a wider blue and lilac band towards the bottom; sections of both bands have faded; red weft.  Lowest section [27 cms] is make up of three equal sized sections of dark blue cloth, broken up with three fine applied red bands, each with a line of white or orange stitching at one edge; blue weft.  All joins hand stitched.
